From equality of the first two flies:
\[
2t \equiv 6t \pmod{1000} \implies 4t \equiv 0 \pmod{1000},
\]
so \(t=250n\) for some integer \(n\).

For the meeting location to be different from the starting point:
\[
2t = 500n \not\equiv 0 \pmod{1000},
\]
so \(n\) must be odd.

Now require the third fly to meet them:
\[
kt \equiv 2t \pmod{1000}
\]
\[
(k-2)t \equiv 0 \pmod{1000}.
\]
Substitute \(t=250n\):
\[
250n(k-2)\equiv 0 \pmod{1000}
\]
\[
1000 \mid 250n(k-2) \implies 4 \mid n(k-2).
\]
Since \(n\) is odd, this is equivalent to
\[
4 \mid k-2.
\]
Thus \(k\equiv 2 \pmod 4\).

Count integers \(k\) with \(7\le k\le 2013\) and \(k\equiv 2\pmod 4\):
\[
10,14,18,\ldots,2010.
\]
Number of terms:
\[
\frac{2010-10}{4}+1 = 501.
\]

\[
\boxed{501}
\]
